slides.title: Member vs Non-Member Overloading
slides.prompt: Why overload binary operator '+' as non-member function when left operand is primitive type (e.g., 'int + Vector')?
options: Member operator requires left operand to be instance of overloaded class
Primitive types cannot be passed by const reference
Member operators cannot return objects by value

slides.title: Operator Precedence Rules
slides.prompt: What happens to operator precedence and associativity when overloaded?
options: They remain identical to built-in operator rules and cannot be changed
Developer can re-define operator precedence levels
All overloaded operators convert to right-to-left associativity
Precedence decreases to lowest priority level
slides.correctAnswer: They remain identical to built-in operator rules and cannot be changed
